\documentclass[11pt]{article}
\usepackage[margin=1in]{geometry}
\usepackage{amsmath}
\input{macros}
\title{Search for Dark Photon Production in Association with a $Z$ Boson}
\author{Analysis Note, Internal Draft}
\date{June 2026}
\begin{document}
\maketitle
\section{Introduction}
Searches for dark photons produced in association with a \Zboson{} boson
are a cornerstone of the hidden-sector programme at the LHC.
The signature considered in this note pairs a leptonically decaying
\Zboson{} boson with large missing transverse momentum, denoted $p_T^{miss}$
in what follows.
The analysis builds on the 2024 dataset, corresponding to an integrated
luminosity of $\lumi = 96~\invfb$.
Compared with the earlier iteration, the signal regions have been
redesigned to improve sensitivity to low-mass dark photons.
\section{Event Selection}
Events are recorded by a suite of triggers requiring either two leptons
or one lepton together with substantial imbalance in the transverse
momentum budget.
The two highest-$p_T$ leptons are required to have transverse momentum
above 30 and 20~GeV and to form an invariant mass within 15~GeV of the
\Zboson{} boson mass.
To suppress top-quark and multi-jet backgrounds, events are required to
satisfy $\ptmiss > 150~\mathrm{GeV}$.
Additional vetoes remove events containing a third lepton or a
$b$-tagged jet.
The residual imbalance requirement $\ptmiss / p_{T}(\Zboson) > 0.6$
further rejects mismeasured multi-jet events.
\section{Background Estimation}
The dominant background, events in which a \Zboson{} boson recoils
against a jet that is poorly measured, is estimated from a control
region inverting the imbalance requirement.
A second control region at low $p_{\mathrm{T}}^{\mathrm{miss}}$,
between 50 and 150~GeV, is used to normalize the diboson contribution.
Transfer factors from the control regions to the signal regions are
taken from simulation and corrected for lepton reconstruction
efficiencies measured in data.
Systematic uncertainties on the transfer factors range from 6 to
14 percent, dominated by the jet energy scale.
\section{Results}
The observed $\ptmiss$ distribution agrees with the background-only
hypothesis across all signal regions.
The largest local excess, 2.1 standard deviations, appears in the bin
with $\ptmiss$ between 250 and 300~GeV and is compatible with the
trial factor of the search.
Exclusion limits at 95 percent confidence level are set on the dark
photon coupling as a function of its mass.
The limits improve on the previous iteration by up to 35 percent for
masses below 40~GeV.
\section{Conclusion}
A search for dark photons produced in association with a \Zboson{}
boson has been performed using the 2024 dataset.
No significant excess is observed in events with the largest $p_T^{miss}$,
and the resulting limits tighten the constraints on low-mass dark photons.
The 2025 dataset, expected to double the integrated luminosity, will
extend the reach of the analysis into unexplored coupling space.
\end{document}

instruction: Our analysis-note style guide now requires one canonical macro for missing transverse momentum, and this note is inconsistent about it: macros.tex defines a legacy \ptmiss, and main.tex mixes \ptmiss calls with hand-written math forms like $p_T^{miss}$ and $p_{\mathrm{T}}^{\mathrm{miss}}$. Please do all three steps: (1) add \newcommand{\met}{p_{\mathrm{T}}^{\mathrm{miss}}} to macros.tex; (2) sweep main.tex so that every math-mode occurrence of the quantity uses \met — the legacy macro calls and the hand-written forms alike; (3) once nothing references it any more, remove the old \ptmiss definition from macros.tex. The other macros (\lumi, \invfb, \Zboson) and every physics number in the note stay exactly as they are.
